Subject: SLO qualification follow-up: throughput & benchmark handoff

Hi Olivia / Acme SRE team,

Thanks again for the time this morning — quick recap and clear asks so we can schedule a reproducible benchmark. High-level items we agreed on and what we need from you: 

- Targets discussed (please confirm):
  - Interactive latency target: p99 <= 300ms (end-to-end, including streaming assembly)
  - Throughput/concurrency: steady sustained 180 RPS, peak bursts to 400 RPS for short windows
  - Streaming window: client-side streaming up to 8s, early token commit behavior required
- Workload signals we need from you:
  - Typical tokens per request (avg and 95th) and response length distribution
  - Expected KV cache hit pattern (cold vs warm) and prefix reuse rate
- Artifacts to share:
  - Canonical prompt set for checkout flows (sample prompts + redact PII)
  - SRE runbook or baseline infra (links are fine)
- Proposed bench plan: Redwood runs a 2-stage harness: warmup (5m), steady-state (10m windows), then a 30m sustained run for cost/latency curves. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, tail-latency, and sustained throughput over 10-minute windows.

Ask: please share the prompt set and any internal SRE constraints by EOD so we can lock the harness and run dates. If procurement needs paperwork before a Dedicated qualification window, loop them in (Ben cc'd).

Attaching a short postcall summary.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Thanks Jordan — good recap. A few clarifications and I'm attaching a small prompt sample bundle to start: checkout-prompts-v1.json (redacted).

Clarifications / numbers from our side:
- Sustained target: we're comfortable with 180 RPS sustained across our peak hours; we expect short bursts up to ~400 RPS (10-30s).
- Streaming latency: target that matters most is p95 end-to-end <= 250ms for our assisted-checkout stream (we can relax p99 if cost trade-offs become extreme).
- Typical tokens: user prompt avg ~40 tokens, model response avg ~120 tokens, 95th token volume ~400 tokens.
- Cache behavior: ~60% prefix reuse for repeat shoppers, but first-touch coldness is significant for new sessions.

SRE runbook: https://acme.example/sre/runbook123 — it has our infra constraints (max worker nodes, allowed test windows, IP allowlist).

Procurement: digging up timelines; I copied procurement@acme-retail.com.

Looping in a few suggested harness parameters and measurement definitions so we have a concrete handoff: 

- Harness configuration (suggested):
  - Warmup: 5 minutes at 50% target load to populate KV caches and JIT kernels
  - Steady-state measurement: 10-minute windows, sample every 10s, run 3 windows per configuration
  - Final run: 30 minute sustained at requested sustained throughput (180 RPS) with bursts simulated every 5 minutes to 400 RPS for 20s to validate tail behavior
- Measurement definitions:
  - p99/p95/p50 are end-to-end latency measured at the gateway (includes serialization + streaming assembly)
  - Throughput reported as completed responses/sec; streaming partial tokens tracked as separate token-rate metric
  - Reproducibility: seed request ids and use canonical prompt set; log raw payloads (redacted) to s3 for audit.
- Infrastructure notes:
  - KV cache warmup recommended between model variant switches (if we test quantized + full FP variants)
  - If ACME's SRE cannot open outgoing peering to Redwood test runners, we can provide an IP allowlist for inbound test traffic or run within your VPC if you prefer.

Attaching a lightweight harness-config.yaml that maps to the above. If we agree on targets, I'll finalize the run script and upload to the Redwood console run.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: harness-config.yaml
